html:
Ernesto "Che" Guevara was an Argentine doctor who became a Marxist revolutionary and a leader of the Cuban Revolution.

Born in Rosario, Argentina, he trained in medicine and travelled across South America by motorbike, a trip he later wrote up as The Motorcycle Diaries. The poverty he saw, and the US backed coup in Guatemala in 1954, turned him to revolution. In Mexico he met Fidel Castro and sailed with him to Cuba in 1956.

He became one of the best guerrilla commanders and won the key battle of Santa Clara in late 1958. In the new government he ran the national bank and the ministry of industry, and he oversaw the execution of many of Batista's men.

He wanted revolution to spread. He fought in the Congo in 1965, then went to Bolivia. There his small band found little support. Bolivian soldiers, helped by the CIA, captured him and shot him in October 1967.

A photograph of him by Alberto Korda, Guerrillero Heroico, became one of the most reproduced images in the world, printed on posters and T-shirts.
sum: Ernesto "Che" Guevara was an Argentine doctor who became a Marxist revolutionary and a leader of the Cuban Revolution.
